scope: Proposition 2.1 of the manuscript “Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras Without Small Spatial Embeddings” (preprints/Near-Inclusions-of-von-Neumann-Algebras-Without-Small-Spatial-Embeddings-October-5-2026/near-inclusions.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 289 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0e3e4d1bbe2ef13b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are unitary representations πz : F → B(K), indexed by z ∈ T, and operators Ak(g) ∈ B(K), indexed by k ∈ Z and g ∈ F, such that πz(g) = ∑︂ k∈Z zk Ak(g), sup g∈F ∥Ak(g)∥ ≤ ck, ck = 1{k=0} + 2t|k| 1 − t , (2.1) πz(sj) WOT − − − → j→∞ tzpe. (2.2) The series in (2.1) converges absolutely in operator norm, uniformly in g and z, and S0 := ∑︂ k∈Z ck < ∞, S1 := ∑︂ k∈Z |k|ck < ∞. (2.3)
